# Resources {.unnumbered}

## Textbooks

1. Kernighan, Brian, and Dennis Ritchie. *The C Programming Language*. 2nd ed. Prentice Hall, 1988. ISBN: 9780131103627. — **the** classic; strongly recommended.
2. Robert W. Sebesta. *Concepts of Programming Languages*. Pearson Education, 2019.
3. Richard Johnsonbaugh and Martin Kalin. *Object-Oriented Programming in C++*. Macmillan USA, 1994.

## Problem Solving (the course's pedagogical spine)

1. G. Pólya. *How to Solve It: A New Aspect of Mathematical Method.* Princeton University Press, 1945 (many later editions). — the four-phase loop we run on every problem: understand → plan → carry out → look back.
2. Arthur Engel. *Problem-Solving Strategies.* Problem Books in Mathematics, Springer, 1998. — the catalog of moves (invariance, working backwards, the extremal principle, …) we name as we meet them.

## Online Material

### The C Programming Laboratory (IIT Jammu lab manual)

📕 [**The C Programming Laboratory**](labs/CLab3_Aroof.pdf) — the department's shared lab
manual for this course: the `vim` editor, the C compilation model (§2.5), variables and
types, the operator **precedence table** (§2.10), and `printf`/`scanf`. Lecture decks and
lab sheets cite it by section number, so it is worth keeping open.

*Prepared by [Aroof Aimen](https://www.iitjammu.ac.in/faculty/~aroofaimen), Dept. of CSE,
IIT Jammu — Laboratory Manual Part II, August 2026. Reproduced here with thanks.*

### MIT OCW 6.087: Practical Programming in C

[MIT OpenCourseWare 6.087 (IAP 2010)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-087-practical-programming-in-c-january-iap-2010/) is an excellent, compact companion to this course, with full lecture notes, labs, and assignments (with solutions):

- [Lecture notes](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-087-practical-programming-in-c-january-iap-2010/pages/lecture-notes/)
- [Labs](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-087-practical-programming-in-c-january-iap-2010/pages/labs/)
- [Assignments](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-087-practical-programming-in-c-january-iap-2010/pages/assignments/)

*Courtesy of MIT OpenCourseWare; used under [CC BY-NC-SA](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/).*

### CS1100: Introduction to Programming (IIT Madras)

Lecture slides from Prof. Shweta Agrawal's CS1100 are mirrored on the [CS1100 lectures page](./cs1100-cse-iitm-2021/index.qmd), reused with permission from Prof. Agrawal and the CSE Department, IIT Madras.

## Tools

| Tool | What for |
|---|---|
| [OnlineGDB](https://www.onlinegdb.com/online_c_compiler) | Write, compile, run, and debug C in the browser |
| [C Tutor](https://pythontutor.com/c.html) | Step-by-step visualization of C program execution |
| [Compiler Explorer](https://godbolt.org/) | See the assembly your C compiles to |
| [USFCA visualizations](https://www.cs.usfca.edu/~galles/visualization/Search.html) | Animated searching/sorting algorithms |
| gcc / clang | Local compilers — setup covered in Lab 1 |
